title: The request and answer shape of the letter-copy handoff, the document type and source the hub assigns, the notice parameters, the P1 recipient field IDs, the payload field names of the event and the notice screen identifier are all unspecified
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1, T3.2 and Appendix T-A; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1, A2.7 and the acceptance criteria; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17, 20 and 42; RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG sections 3 and 12.4; RWB-P5-E1032-CON
section: Preconditions; Exception paths; Data 11; Contract 12.1, 12.2 and 12.3; Screens and states 15
description: Seven values the story needs have no source, and each is written in the story as a placeholder instead of a guess. (a) The exact request and answer field names of the P5 generated-document operation, and whether the hub answers with the intake item or only with the document it stored: the Ownership Map fixes the path and the owner but no source fixes the payload. (b) The document type code and the source value the hub assigns to a letter copy: source GENERATED is named for a generated document in FSD P6 A2.7, but no source says which document type a notice letter copy takes. (c) The names of the notice parameters the DP-06 read would use: the P6 FSD and TSD declare no notice parameter at all. (d) The BR field IDs of the P1 party and contact-point values the copy merges. (e) The payload field names of rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1 beyond the IDs and values named in the event catalogue row. (f) The message that is shown when the hub refuses a copy, where the shared message set offers only MSG-GEN-006 naming a system. (g) The screen identifier of the notice panel that shows the notice with its copy. A build team cannot finalise the client, the event schema or the message set from the sources as they stand.
evidence: ownership.json api row POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents (owner P5) gives the path only; TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1 lists eleven operations in the legacy base and none for a generated letter copy; FSD P6 A2.7 names source GENERATED for a generated contract document only; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 lists no notice parameter; the P6 FSD grep for parameter returns payment matching rows only; Architecture v5 slide 42 row 13 gives the event name, the topic and the consumer only
proposed: Publish the generated-document request and answer of P5 with the intake item it creates, name the document type and source a notice letter copy takes, register the notice parameters with their names, extend the event catalogue row to its payload, and allocate the notice screen identifier

title: The DP-added platform and P3 contracts are missing from the story dependency rows
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19; WP B-P6-05 story line for RWB-P6-E1032-APP (Depends on (build) None; Contract dependencies RWB-P5-E1032-CON)
description: The pattern set of this story is DP01, DP03, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP15 and DP19, and the DP table attaches a platform H and, for two patterns, a P3 C to seven of them: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON for parameters, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON for reference data, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON for the outbox and inbox, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON for the workflow kit, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON for the Flyway sequence and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the gateway route. The plan's rows give Depends on (build) as None and Contract dependencies as RWB-P5-E1032-CON only, so nine contracts the story compiles against are absent from the build graph, and Ready to start stays Day 1 although the workflow kit and the outbox library are wave 0 work.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 rows DP-03 (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), DP-06 (H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON), DP-07 (H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON), DP-09 (H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), DP-10 (H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), DP-15 (H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON), DP-19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON); WP B-P6-05 line for RWB-P6-E1032-APP gives H [] and C [RWB-P5-E1032-CON]

title: No source describes the letter copy becoming an intake item at the document hub, and FSD P6 keeps a generated document as a stored document on the case
source: RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG sections 2, 3 and 12.4; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.7 and AC-P6-007-01; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 (rwb-comms OUT: Document generate letter) and slide 15 (rwb-document IN: POST /documents/generate); Ownership Map api row POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents
description: The integration story of the key asserts that the letter copy generated in NoticeDispatchWorkflow becomes an intake item, and it names the copy as one of the three intake sources of the wave 1 proof. No source in the set states how that happens: the P6 FSD treats a generated document as a stored document on the case with source GENERATED, a state and a write-once flag, and the P5 story of the key treats an intake item as a scan, a partner result or a classified upload. Neither document says whether the hub creates an intake item from a generated document, whether rwb-comms supplies the case ID so that the item can be matched without OCR, or whether the copy is attached directly. This story therefore fixes only what it owns — the copy, the case, the template version and the document ID — and leaves the item's creation, matching and attach to P5, which is where the sources put them.
evidence: RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG section 12.4 row rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1 ('The letter copy is generated and becomes an intake item') and section 3; FSD P6 AC-P6-007-01 stores a generated document with source GENERATED, state DRAFT and write_once false; Architecture v5 slide 17 gives rwb-comms OUT 'Document: generate letter' as a Temporal call and slide 15 gives rwb-document IN POST /documents/generate; no source describes an intake item created from a generated document
proposed: State in the P5 and P6 contract documents, and in the service contract catalogue, whether the hub creates an intake item from a generated document and which fields of the request it needs, so that the handoff and the item are specified once

title: The P6 module declares no notice parameter, so DP-06 has no named value to read
source: FSD P6 Communications v3 (grep for parameter returns only payment matching rows); TSD P6 Communications v2 (no parameter table); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-06; FSD P6 BR-P6-001
description: DP-06 is in the pattern set, and every module value a business person may change must be a parameter row read through the parameters contract of rwb-case. The P6 FSD and TSD declare no parameter of the communications module at all: the only parameter references in the FSD belong to payment matching, which is not this service's content. The story keeps the parameters read wired because the pattern requires the path, and it invents no parameter name; a build team cannot tell from the sources which notice value is tunable, and the letter copy is the first flow in the service that would need one.
evidence: FSD P6 Communications v3 lines naming a parameter are AC-EXC-P6-010-05, AC-EXC-P6-010-07 and AC-EXC-P6-011-05, all payment matching; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 lists notice, template, merge_field and signature_request only and T3.2 lists value lists only; FSD P6 BR-P6-001 states the principle without naming a value
proposed: Name the business-owned values of the communications module in a parameter catalog row with their defaults, or state that the module has none and that DP-06 applies to it as a path without a value

title: The legacy access case and the legacy attach cases have no subject in rwb-comms, so the carried test cases prove the notice read instead
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-032 section 16 (TC-E1-032-16 and TC-E1-032-17); RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG section 2 (legacy AC1 to AC15 sit with RWB-P5-E1032-APP; the access and resilience criteria sit with the sibling APP stories); WP B-P6-05 tcs_legacy list
section: Story 1; Exception paths X11; Test cases 16
description: The legacy access case attaches an unmatched item and expects MSG-P4-002, and the fifteen attach cases assert the match status, the candidates and the stored document — all of which belong to rwb-document in the target. The WP keeps the seventeen legacy case IDs on this story, so each is carried with its legacy fixture but the subject changes: the access case proves the notice-read refusal of this service, which is the right the P6 matrix grants and the one the monolith refused, and the other fifteen prove the P6 side of the same fixture, namely that the copy is handed over once and that rwb-comms stores no match status, no candidate and no review decision. The gap is recorded because the identity of the cases changed and a test lead reading the legacy case would not recognise it.
evidence: Legacy story RWB-E1-032 section 16 rows TC-E1-032-01 to TC-E1-032-16; RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG section 2 and section 19 (the five APP builds); WP B-P6-05 tcs_legacy list for RWB-P6-E1032-APP; TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.2 (API-P6-002 requires the Litigation read right)
proposed: Record in the test case register that the attach proof of TC-E1-032-01 to TC-E1-032-15 is owned by RWB-P5-E1032-APP and that the P6 copy proves the service side, and note the access case as the notice-read refusal

title: The event catalogue names rwb-decision as the only consumer of NoticeGenerated, while the document hub is expected to turn the copy into an intake item
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 row 13 (NoticeGenerated, producer rwb-comms, topic rwb.comms.events.v1, consumers rwb-decision); slide 17 (rwb-comms OUT: Document generate letter); RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG section 12.4
description: The event catalogue gives rwb-decision as the only consumer of rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1, and the architecture puts the letter generation on the call edge from rwb-comms to rwb-document. The integration story, written against the same architecture, treats the copy that becomes an intake item as the evidence of the chain and waits on the same event. The two mechanisms are not reconciled: if the hub learned of the copy from the event it would be a second consumer, and if it learns from the call then the event is a notification for rwb-decision only. This story takes the second reading, keeps the event payload free of any document content, and states the consumer set of the catalogue row so that a hub consumer would be a catalogue change and not a silent one.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42 row 13 consumers column holds rwb-decision only; slide 17 gives rwb-comms OUT 'Document: generate letter' and no event to rwb-document; RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG section 12.4 lists rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1 with the use 'the letter copy is generated and becomes an intake item'
proposed: Decide once whether the document hub consumes rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1 or is called by rwb-comms, and align the event catalogue row, the P5 story and the integration suite to that decision

title: The base documents of the story are in review, not approved
source: FSD P6 Communications v3 document control (Status In review, 15 November 2026); TSD P6 Communications v2 document control (Status In review, 28 October 2026); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: The FSD and TSD of the module are both at status In review at the versions this story is written from, and no approved version of either exists in the source set. The story therefore carries the status Draft (realignment v1) and builds against the reviewed versions as they stand. No field, table, operation or rule used by the story changes between a reviewed and an approved version of these two documents as far as the source set shows, but a build team cannot claim an approved baseline.
evidence: FSD P6 Communications v3 document control row Status = In review; TSD P6 Communications v2 document control row Status = In review; no approved version of either file appears in the extract folder
proposed: Approve the FSD and TSD of the module, or record that the wave 1 build uses the reviewed versions and that any change in the approved text is a change request

title: The values the rescan notice needs are not named in any source
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 049 OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub v1.md sections 3, 12, 13 and 14; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1.3.1 and A2.3.4.3; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1, T3.2 and A.2
description: The story builds the rescan notice, and eight of its values are given by no source: (a) the template code, version, language and body of the rescan notice template, which the legacy places in the ACE notification path under the name recovery templates without a code; (b) the notice type of an operational rescan notice, for which LOV-NOTICE has no value; (c) the property list of the Notice answer of API-P6-002, for which the TSD names the resource only; (d) the request and result shape of the ACE notification path; (e) the recipient reference passed to that path, whether the case owner user reference or a contact point token; (f) the retry count and interval beyond the single retry the criterion asserts, and the attempt limit and exception rule that follow it; (g) the state values of a notification-path dispatch and any hold reason other than TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN; (h) the name of the feature flag of the capability. Each is written in the story as the placeholder of Template and Rules v1 section R9 and none is invented.
evidence: RWB-E1-049 section 13: "Notification template for MSG-P5-018 in the ACE notification path, recovery templates." with no code or version. TSD P6 v2 T-A.2 API-P6-002: "| Response | Notice |" with no property list. TSD P6 v2 T3.2 LOV-NOTICE: "DEMAND, RECALL, STATUTORY_SALE_NOTICE, GUARANTOR_NOTICE" and no operational value. FSD P6 v3 A2.3.4.3 AC-EXC-P6-003-03: "after the retry limit of 5 the send is in the exception queue under rule R-UNI-34" with no interval. TSD P6 v2 T3.1 DF-LEG-032 hold_reason has "None" in the List column.
proposed: Settle the eight values at the baseline review of the capability: publish the rescan notice template row with its code, version, language, body and channel, extend LOV-NOTICE with the value the business owner chooses, baseline the Notice answer and the notification-path request and result with the platform integration owner, and set the retry values and the state list as data rows. The placeholders stay in the story until each value is published, and each one closes with the row that publishes it (ASM-B-P6-05-E1049-1, ASM-B-P6-05-E1049-4, ASM-B-P6-05-E1049-6, ASM-B-P6-05-E1049-7, ASM-B-P6-05-E1049-8 and ASM-B-P6-05-E1049-13).

title: The document rescan event that triggers the notice is in no event catalogue and has no name or payload
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42 and 43 (event catalogue); Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 049 sections 4 and 12; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 049 (in-process rescan notifier)
description: The legacy story sends MSG-P5-018 from the OCR step of the document job in the same process, so no event exists. In the target the notice is a different service from the OCR step, so one event on the topic of the document service is the only trigger that keeps the two services decoupled. The event catalogue of Architecture v5 lists DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted for rwb-document and no rescan event, and no source gives the name, the payload, the topic element or the producer contract of such an event. The story therefore builds against a proposed name and a proposed element list on the topic the Ownership Map gives the owner, and cannot be built or tested end to end until the producing service publishes it.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42: "| 16 | DocumentStored | rwb-document | rwb.document.events.v1 | rwb-agent, rwb-case |" and "| 17 | DocumentFieldsExtracted | rwb-document | rwb.document.events.v1 | rwb-case |" and no rescan row. RWB-E1-049 section 4 step 8: "OcrStep: for an item in RESCAN with a known case, sends MSG-P5-018 to the case owner through the ACE notification path" inside the same job. Architecture v5 slide 17 gives rwb-comms no document event as an IN element.
proposed: Publish the event as rwb.document.OcrRescanRequested.v1 on rwb.document.events.v1, produced by P5 rwb-document in the same transaction as the intake item state change, with the element list intakeItemId, documentId, caseId (absent when no case), rescanPages, quality, languages and occurredAt, and add it to the event catalogue and to RWB-P5-E1049-CON. Until it is published the listener builds against the proposed envelope and its fake.

title: The build and contract dependency lists of the plan do not carry the dependencies the DP table adds to this key
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md section R5.5 (DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15, DP-19); _work/msr/wp/B-P6-05.md story line RWB-P6-E1049-APP; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api rows GET /cases/{caseId}
description: The plan gives this story no build dependency and one contract dependency, RWB-P5-E1049-CON, and the metadata keeps those lists. The pattern table the story applies adds six build dependencies (RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and two contract dependencies (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON). The read of the case number and the owner through the rwb-case contract adds a third contract dependency of the same class, and the plan carries no row for it either. The story declares all of them in sections 3 and 13 so it can build on Day 1, and the plan's lists therefore understate the dependency set of the key.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5: DP-06 "H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON", DP-07 "H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON", DP-09 "H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON", DP-10 "H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON", DP-15 "H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON", DP-19 "H RWB-PLT-N001-CON". WP B-P6-05 story line: "\"H\": [], \"C\": [\"RWB-P5-E1049-CON\"]". Ownership Map api row "GET /cases/{caseId}" owner P3 with no contract identifier.
proposed: Update the plan and the dependency map for this key to the DP table: six H rows and three C rows, and keep the metadata of the written story as the plan states it until the plan is corrected. The Day-1 rule is unaffected because every H row is a platform contract story.

title: The notice list of values has no value for an operational rescan notice
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2 (LOV-NOTICE); Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-018); Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1 and A2.3; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 049 section 14
description: The notice row carries notice_type from LOV-NOTICE, whose four values are DEMAND, RECALL, STATUTORY_SALE_NOTICE and GUARANTOR_NOTICE. All four are customer notices with a legal or collection effect. The rescan message of the legacy story is an operational message to the case owner of the bank, sent on the same service and through the same notification path, and none of the four values describes it. Writing one of them on the row would misstate the notice in the decision record and on the screen, and the sources give no fifth value.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.2: "| LOV-NOTICE | DEMAND, RECALL, STATUTORY_SALE_NOTICE, GUARANTOR_NOTICE |". TSD P6 v2 T3.1: "DF-LEG-018 | notice_type | LOV | varchar(25) | Yes | LOV-NOTICE". RWB-E1-049 section 14 MSG-P5-018: "Page {page} of {document} on case {case} could not be read. Scan it again and send it to the document hub." and section 10: "RW-CASEOWN | Receives the rescan notice for their case".
proposed: Add one value to LOV-NOTICE for an operational notice to the case owner, named by the business owner and loaded as a reference row, and set DF-LEG-018 from it. The criteria of this story assert the message, the case, the document and the dispatch facts and not the notice type, so the placeholder closes without a rewrite of a criterion.

title: The document token of the rescan message has no named reference form
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 049 section 14 (MSG-P5-018); Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-017); Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1
description: MSG-P5-018 says "Page {page} of {document} on case {case} could not be read" and the story must fill the document token from the document read of rwb-document, but no source says whether the token carries the file name, the document type name, the document title or the document identifier. The token decides what the case owner reads and whether two notices about one document read the same, so it is a wording decision and not a formatting one, and it cannot be fixed from a source.
evidence: RWB-E1-049 section 14: "| MSG-P5-018 | A page is below the quality threshold on a document of a known case | Page {page} of {document} on case {case} could not be read. Scan it again and send it to the document hub. |". TSD P6 v2 T3.1 notice: "DF-LEG-017 | document_id | CROSS_REF | uuid | No".
proposed: Fill the token from the document read of rwb-document with the display reference that contract returns, and with the document identifier where it returns none, so one document always reads the same; record the decision in the baseline of the message text and change no criterion.

title: Template code, channel, notice type, field names, recipient role holders, guard right and retry window are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 063 Agent monitoring dashboard v1 E2c v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 12, 13, 14 and 15); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3.md (A2.1, A2.3, A2.4, A2.5 and A2.6); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2.md (T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2 API-P6-002 and API-P6-008); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-ITG-W1 Wave 1 integration/RWB ITG E1063 ITG Agent monitoring dashboard v1 [E2c] - integration v1.md (section 12.2 and assumption ASM-B-ITG-W1-08-E1063-4); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 17, 20, 41, 42 and 44)
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story names a notification template called agent cost alert for MSG-P10-004 in the P6 template set and sends the message to the policy alert role and to RW-RISK, but no source read here gives the template code, its language, its body, its version, the delivery channel (SMS, LINE or letter), the notice type value the cost alert is stored under, the column names of the new notice fields, the list of role holders behind RW-COE and RW-RISK, the right that guards a read of the cost-alert notice, or the retry window and attempt limit of the outbox relay. The notice-type list LOV-NOTICE of the module specification carries DEMAND, RECALL, STATUTORY_SALE_NOTICE and GUARANTOR_NOTICE only, so the cost alert has no list entry. evidence: RWB-E1-063 sections 3 (template and alert role of the policy), 4 step 5 (MSG-P10-004 through the P6 notification interface), 5 X5 (sent_at empty and the JOB-11 retry), 7 AC2 and AC7, 12 (published interface used by JOB-15, events published: none), 13 (Notification template agent cost alert for MSG-P10-004 in the P6 template set; feature flag rwb.agent.monitor) and 14 (MSG-P10-004 text); FSD P6 A2.3 to A2.6 (template withdrawn and conduct check messages, retry limit 5 and R-UNI-34) and TSD P6 T3.2 LOV-NOTICE and LOV-CHANNEL, T-A.2 API-P6-002 and API-P6-008 (purpose, errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503, Idempotency-Key, no request or answer field list); Architecture v5 slides 17 (P6 IN and OUT), 20 (the notification path through ACE Common), 41 (rwb_comms owns notices, templates and merge fields), 42 (NoticeGenerated and NoticeDispatched) and 44 (JOB-11 every minute in every service).
owner_role: P6 comms owner, P10 agent owner and platform notification path owner
proposed: Seed the template code, the channel, the notice type and the retry window as parameter and reference rows plus service configuration, keep the MSG-P10-004 text unchanged, publish the request and answer fields of the two operations in the P6 contract, and declare the guard right of the cost-alert notice read at gateway-bff, as set out in ASM-B-P6-05-E1063-4.

title: The legacy data lake copy and the agent monitoring dashboard have no target, and P6 has no replacement for the dashboard
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 063 Agent monitoring dashboard v1 E2c v1.md (sections 2, 3, 4, 7, 12 and 15); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 30, 37 and 41); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (section R5.5 DP-17); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-ITG-W1 Wave 1 integration/RWB ITG E1063 ITG Agent monitoring dashboard v1 [E2c] - integration v1.md (sections 2, 7 AC8, 12.7 and 19)
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story reaches the dashboard by copying the daily agent run figures to the data lake table agent_run_daily inside JOB-15 at 01:30, matching the row count and the sum of runs against the source, and letting the Power BI report Agent monitor v1 read the copy and not the live tables (REQ-DRI-009). Arch v5 slide 37 replaces the data lake and Power BI feed (INT-19/20) with reports from rwb-reporting, and DP-17 records the removal with no dependency added. The legacy agent_run_daily table therefore has no target, the Power BI page has no source, and the dashboard read is a P9 rwb-reporting read model built from rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1 and the P10 daily step. Nothing in the sources names a dashboard deliverable that stays in P6, so the rwb-comms slice carries the cost-alert notification only and builds no dashboard, no copy and no measure.
evidence: RWB-E1-063 section 2 (copies daily agent run figures to the data lake, the Power BI dashboard reads the copy), section 3 (RWB-E1-014 nightly copy path, RW-BIANAL builds the Power BI report on the data lake table), section 4 steps 4 and 6 (writes agent_run_daily and checks the row count and run sum; opens the Power BI report), section 7 AC1, AC3 and AC4, section 12 (output data lake table agent_run_daily with its thirteen columns), section 13 (Agent monitor v1 Power BI report, migration V10_006__agent_alert.sql) and section 15 (the report in the Workbench reporting workspace with loaded and stale states); Arch v5 slide 37 (today: data lake and Power BI feed INT-19/20; proposed: removed, reports from rwb-reporting) and slide 41 (P9 rwb-reporting owns measures, snapshots, steering dashboard and regulatory reports; P6 rwb-comms owns notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-17; RWB-E1-014 is retired under Template and Rules v1 section R6.
owner_role: P6 comms owner, P9 reporting owner and architecture owner

title: The agent alert event name, the alert notification operation name and the non-case binding of the cost alert are not named for the target

description: The legacy story raises the cost alert inside JOB-15 and then calls the P6 notification interface in the same step, so there is no event and no operation name to carry over. title: RWB-P6-E1073-APP: the local copy table and its columns, the parameter read path, the two added check names and the local run record are not specified in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 20, 27 and 41); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 14, 15 and 16); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (tables; rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case to P7); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 073 Rule authoring validation test scenarios approval and rollback in Drools v1.md (sections 3, 11, 12, 13 and 16); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2.md (T3.1 and T5.2)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.4 Events consumed; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: Several values this story needs are given by no source in the read set. (a) The local evaluated copy is named but never described: no source gives its table name, its columns, its state values or where the last good copy is kept across a restart, so the migration V1073_1 and the LocalCopyRepository cannot be written from a document, and the Ownership Map carries no such table. (b) The parameters rules.testcases.min (50) and drools.kiebase.cache.max (20) are read through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06), but neither the parameter codes as catalog rows nor the read path of that contract appears in the sources, so a test can only assert against a fake. (c) A local load refusal reuses MSG-P3-027, whose {check} value is compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row or scenario in the legacy story; the local checksum and package-state refusals add two values and no source names them, and the message prefix of the refusal is not given either. (d) The scenario set stored with a version travels to the evaluating service in no documented shape, and where the local run record of a refusal is persisted is not stated. (e) The 300 ms budget of NFR-011 does not say whether it is measured around the activity call, the evaluate call inside it or the whole workflow step. Every one of these is carried as a placeholder in the story and read as an assumption; none changes a legacy value, a message text or a version label.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 27 (the owning service loads the model, verifies the checksum, swaps it atomically and runs the rules inside an activity under 300 ms; no shared rule server); slide 20 (every service writes its own schema with outbox, inbox and decision_record); slide 41 (rwb_comms schema and rwb-comms queue, P6 owns notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery); Temporal and Drools design slide 14 (EvaluateRules and RecordAndApply run inside an activity), slide 15 (GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, checksum verified, swap in, rollback one call) and slide 16 (KieBaseRegistry holds one KieBase per package version with an LRU of 20; the record carries ruleId and ruleVersion); Ownership Map tables (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case are P7's, and no local-copy table exists); legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 3 (rules.testcases.min = 50 and drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20 through RWB-E1-042), 11, 12 and 13 (one recovery schema, rule_package_version and a Blob workbook), and section 14 (MSG-P3-027 with the six {check} values); TSD P6 v2 T3.1 (notice, template, merge_field and signature_request only) and T5.2 (P6 calls P7 for the decision log); Template and Rules v1 section R9.
area: Local rule copy, data and contract detail
proposed: Fix the five points in the wave-1 design at the rwb-decision and rwb-comms contract review and record them in the DB stories: the local copy table name and columns, the two parameter rows and their read path, the two added {check} values with their message text, the shape in which the scenario set and its local run result travel and are stored, and the measurement point of the 300 ms budget. Until then the story keeps the legacy values unchanged (50 scenarios, cache 20, MSG-P3-027, MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003) and builds against fakes.

title: RWB-P6-E1073-APP: the DP-04 row of the pattern table names H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON while the plan gives no H and C RWB-P3-E1073-CON
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (section R5.5, DP-04 row, and section R5.4 dependency classes); _work/msr/wp/B-P6-05.md (story line RWB-P6-E1073-APP: H [], C [RWB-P3-E1073-CON]); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 14, 27 and 41); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 15 and 16); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-ITG-W1 Wave 1 integration/RWB ITG E1073 ITG Rule authoring, validation, test scenarios, approval and rollback in Drools - integration v1.md (sections 3, 10 and 12.2)
section: Metadata (Depends on (build); Contract dependencies); 3 Preconditions; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: Two sources disagree about this story's dependencies. The DP-04 row of the pattern table adds H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON (the embedded Drools kit, a platform CON of wave 0) and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON (the rule package contract of rwb-decision) to every story that applies the pattern. The plan line for RWB-P6-E1073-APP gives Depends on (build) = None and Contract dependencies = RWB-P3-E1073-CON, so it carries no H at all and cites a P3 contract instead of the P7 one, while RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 3 and section 12.2 name RWB-P7-E1073-APP as the owner of the model fetch and of RulePackageInForce. Two readings follow: either the plan's P3 row is the contract this story must fake and the kit is a prerequisite outside the dependency list, or the DP-04 row is right and both a platform H and a P7 C belong on the story. evidence: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-04 row (H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON) and section R5.4 (H blocks only on a non-CON story of the same lane; C never blocks); WP B-P6-05 story line (patterns include DP04; H []; C [RWB-P3-E1073-CON]; ready Day 1); Arch v5 slide 27 (governance in rwb-decision, evaluation local), slide 14 (P7 IN: POST /rule-models and GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}) and slide 41 (P7 owns the DMN model registry, P6 owns notices and templates); Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (each owning service fetches the model with GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}) and slide 16 (KieBaseRegistry per service); RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 3 (the admin paths and the model fetch are RWB-P7-E1073-APP), section 10 (rwb-comms owns the local copy and the evaluation of the package it is assigned) and section 12.2 (GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{n}/{v}, P7, not in the Ownership Map or API Specification v4).
proposed: Keep the plan's Metadata rows as written (Depends on (build) None, Contract dependencies RWB-P3-E1073-CON), treat RWB-PLT-E1072-CON as a platform prerequisite delivered by the wave-0 train and RWB-P7-E1073-CON as the contract that the model fetch fake stands in for, and correct the DP-04 row or the plan at the next rules-of-record pass so one of the two stops disagreeing with the other.

title: RWB-P6-E1073-APP: the model fetch operation, its path segments, its request fields and its response fields are not specified in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 14 and 27); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 15 and 16); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api section); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-ITG-W1 Wave 1 integration/RWB ITG E1073 ITG Rule authoring, validation, test scenarios, approval and rollback in Drools - integration v1.md (sections 12.2 and 12.8)

description: The service has to fetch the model of a package version, verify its checksum and compile it, and the only description of that operation is the path family GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} on Arch v5 slides 14 and 27 and in the Temporal and Drools design slide 15. No source states the two path segments in words (a package code and a version label, a package code and a numeric suffix, or two identifiers), the media type of the answer, whether the model travels as generated DRL, as a workbook reference or both, whether the checksum is a header or a body field, how the version state and the valid from date are returned so a local load can refuse a version that is not APPROVED, or how a refusal is coded. The Ownership Map has no row for the operation and API Specification v4 does not carry it, so its name, its request fields and its response fields are placeholders in this story and the fake is built from the arguments of the design.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14 (P7 IN: REST POST /rule-models and GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}) and slide 27 (Load: GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, verify checksum, swap in); Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (each owning service fetches with GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}), slide 16 (RuleResult carries packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId and outputs) and the version state list (LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED); Ownership Map api section (no rule-models row); RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 12.2 (the path is named on Arch v5 slide 27, is not in the Ownership Map or API Specification v4, and is carried as CG-B-ITG-W1-10-E1073-1 and ASM-B-ITG-W1-10-E1073-2) and section 12.8 (no fake for it at integration level).
proposed: Publish the model fetch in the rwb-decision API document and the wave-1 contract story before the build: method GET, the base /api/recovery/decision/v1, the two path segments as packageCode and versionLabel, an answer that carries the generated DRL, the SHA-256 checksum, the version state and the valid from date, a 404 for an unknown label and a 409 for a version that is not loadable, all under the 2 s client budget and one hop; until then the story builds against a WireMock fake of that shape.

proposed: Load the escalation template as one row of the rwb-comms template catalogue with the message ID MSG-P7-011, the two placeholders {decision} and {caseNo}, a channel from LOV-CHANNEL and an Approved version, and read the retry from the platform outbox policy of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; the template code and the channel value are agreed at the wave 2 design review, and the story builds against the assumed values of ASM-B-P6-05-E2013-1 until they are loaded.

title: The event catalogue lists gateway-bff as the only consumer of ApprovalRequested and carries no ApprovalEscalated event, yet this story also consumes the event for the escalation notice
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 (events 09 and 19) against the Temporal and Drools design (workflow kit, approval) and legacy RWB-E2-013 step 9
description: Architecture v5 slide 42 gives ApprovalRequested (event 09, rwb.decision.events.v1) exactly one consumer, gateway-bff (inbox), and gives TimerBreached (event 19, rwb.case.events.v1) the same single consumer; no ApprovalEscalated, ApprovalPassedUp or escalation event exists on any topic in the catalogue. Legacy RWB-E2-013 step 9 escalates on EV-19 TimerBreached through a listener of the approval module, so in the target either the escalation reaches rwb-comms as a re-published ApprovalRequested, as this story reads it, or the catalogue gains a consumer and an event it does not have. The story keeps the published event and adds no event of its own; the conflict is recorded so the catalogue and the AsyncAPI document are corrected by their owners and not silently by a story.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 rows 09 (ApprovalRequested, consumers 'gateway-bff (inbox)') and 19 (TimerBreached, consumers 'gateway-bff (inbox)'); slide 14 rwb-decision OUT topic rwb.decision.events.v1 (ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce); legacy RWB-E2-013 section 4 step 9 and section 5 X1; section 12.4 of this story
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-013 section 4 step 9, section 5 X1 and section 12 (Events)
proposed: Keep the published event: rwb-decision re-publishes rwb.decision.ApprovalRequested.v1 with the escalation level raised and the new due time, and rwb-comms is added as a consumer of that event in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog and in the rwb-decision AsyncAPI document; do not invent ApprovalEscalated, and keep TimerBreached a legacy reference because the breach is a durable timer inside ApprovalWorkflow.

title: No source names the notice and message operations or the notice fields that carry an approval reference, an escalation level, a recipient and a sent time
source: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 and T-A.1 (API-P6-002 and API-P6-008) against legacy RWB-E2-013 section 13 and the MSG-P7-011 notification
description: The legacy story asks rwb-comms to send MSG-P7-011 to the new approver and says nothing about the record of that send. TSD P6 v2 defines one notice table with a notice type, a template, a party, a barcode, a sent date, a delivery status and a hold reason, and it has no column for an approval reference, an escalation level, a recipient role, a recipient user reference or a send time distinct from the WIN sent date; its two operations are a notice request for a case and a notice read. API-P6-008 is documented as a customer SMS or LINE message with a party, a template, a language and a conduct check, not as an internal notification to an approver. The story therefore keeps the two published paths, fills the notice with the escalation kind and names the fields it needs, and records that the shapes are a contract-baseline decision confirmed at the contract review.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 notice (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023 and DF-LEG-030 to DF-LEG-034) and template/merge_field; T-A.1 API-P6-002 GET /notices/{noticeId} and API-P6-008 POST /cases/{caseId}/messages; FSD P6 v3 A2.3 and A2.4 (the message request of a party); legacy RWB-E2-013 section 13 and section 14 MSG-P7-011
proposed: Keep GET /notices/{noticeId} and POST /cases/{caseId}/messages on base /api/recovery/comms/v1, with the Notice and MessageRequest field sets of section 12.1 of the story, and let the contract review of rwb-comms confirm or rename them; the migration V2013_1 and the unique key on the approval reference and the escalation level follow the confirmed shape.
